errors.english: Because a discerning person seeks for the sake of spiritual practice
errors.why: The knower is the one sought (jñānavān mṛgyate): one who possesses knowledge is sought out for the sake of practice; he is not the one seeking.

fix.find: Because a discerning person seeks for the sake of spiritual practice
fix.replace: Because one who possesses knowledge is sought for the sake of what is to be practised

errors.english: Showing how omniscience itself without reasoning cannot be known
errors.why: The Tibetan says omniscience itself is not the criterion (by which the teacher is to be recognised), not that omniscience cannot be known without reasoning.

note: Follows the Pramāṇavārttika argument on the teacher's knowledge reasonably, but the key root line is turned around (the knower is sought, not seeking) and some argumentative clauses are muddled.

errors.why: The point is a fortiori about those spat-out foods themselves (if even the ground they touch is impure, what need to speak of them), not about other things.

note: A faithful and readable rendering of the Catuḥśataka commentary on the impurity of the body, with only a small slip of reference.

errors.english: Alternatively, to state that the distinction is contradictory without cessation
errors.why: སྲོད་པ (= སྡོད་པ, 'persisting', cf. བསྡད་ནས above and སྡོད་པའི་ཕྱོགས on the next side) gives the alternative in which the opposed things do not persist; it is not 'cessation'.

fix.find: Alternatively, to state that the distinction is contradictory without cessation
fix.replace: Alternatively, to state that, without [the things] persisting, its distinction is the contradiction

errors.english: The response to the idea that the distinction between cause and effect constitutes the contradiction
errors.why: This is the author's own answer: the contradiction is the very distinction of cause and effect that operates after persisting (བསྡད་ནས, dropped in the English); it is not a reply to that idea.

errors.english: If the cause is incapable and thus produces nothing, how does it cause the reversal?
errors.why: The objection is that fire, since it produces (the incapable moment of cold), is a producer, so how can it be a remover; not that the cause produces nothing.

note: The fire-and-cold virodha discussion is followed in outline, but the two alternatives (with and without persistence) and several objection/answer joints are misread.

errors.english: through the power of disciples' prayers
errors.why: BCA 9.36 vineyapraṇidhānābhyām: by the force of the disciples and of the (Buddha's former) vow, two factors, not the disciples' prayers.

note: A sound verse rendering of Bodhicaryāvatāra IX on mind-only, emptiness-imprints and the wish-gem simile, with one familiar misreading.
A faithful lemma-by-lemma rendering of the Madhyamakāvatāra commentary on form and mind existing conventionally.

errors.english: Not repeatedly with the shoulder, the head, or the waist.
errors.why: ཡང་ཡང here means 'even a light one', as the commentary makes explicit (ཁུར་ཡང་དུ་ཟིན་ཀྱང་); it does not mean 'repeatedly'.

fix.find: Not repeatedly with the shoulder, the head, or the waist.
fix.replace: Not even a light one with the shoulder, the head, or the waist.

errors.english: The lower end of the (shamthap) monastic lower robe should be untied.
errors.why: The stated purpose is to keep the private parts restrained (གསང་བ་བསྡམས་པ), so the rule is to knot the lower end of the robe, not untie it; the same applies to the commentary sentence.

note: A clear rendering of the Vinaya verses and commentary on shaving, the barber's order and deportment, with a misread 'light load' and a doubtful 'untie'.

errors.english: then the universal one line of text follows
errors.why: The side ends with 'the universal' mid-sentence; 'one line of text follows' is a stray note, not a translation.

fix.find: then the universal one line of text follows

errors.english: Even so, the exclusion (vyavrtti) the turning away or negation of other possibilities does not become a universal in itself.
errors.why: The negation goes with the closing འགའ་ཞིག་ཡོད་པའི་ཕྱིར་ནི་མ་ཡིན་ནོ: the exclusion is called a universal, but not because some positive entity exists; the English makes the commentary deny that the exclusion is a universal.

note: A sound rendering of the apoha passage with helpful glosses, apart from a stray note at the end and one negation attached to the wrong clause.
Translates the Tibetan verses of the bilingual Avadānakalpalatā side accurately (the opening half-verse is obscure in the Tibetan), with the Sanskrit lines treated as the same text.

errors.why: འགོ is a slip for འགྲོ ('world, beings'), as the commentary glosses with འགྲོ་བ་འཇིག་རྟེན་འཛམ་བུའི་གླིང་འདིར.

errors.english: If it is reversed, then peace will be attained.
errors.why: In the verse ཞི་བ means the lamp goes out (is extinguished) once the Vinaya ceases, as the commentary says (ནུབ་པ); 'peace will be attained' reads as a good outcome.

errors.english: Regarding the term perfect, it refers to purity
errors.why: 'Complete' here means being whole (ཚང་བ) enough to carry out the motions and formal acts of the saṅgha; it does not mean purity.

errors.english: [note: meaning, if its time runs out or it is fully practiced to its end]
errors.why: The sense is that the Vinaya ceases or loses its capacity, after which the lamp of Dharma goes out; 'fully practiced to its end' suggests the opposite.

note: Generally follows the praise of the Vinaya, but the key verse on the Dharma lamp is misread in several places (beginning/world, peace/extinction, purity/completeness).

errors.english: The directions are thoroughly permeated from above.
errors.why: This continues the earthquake description: the (northern) quarters rise upward; nothing is 'permeated from above'.

errors.english: as the divine command had instructed
errors.why: In the drama ལྷ (deva) is the form of address for the king, so the line means 'as His Majesty commanded', not a divine command.

errors.english: this great house in the manner of admitting everyone
errors.why: ཚུལ་ཁང་པ is an almshouse (sattra) open to all, and the same word is behind 'ritual house' later; it is not 'in the manner of'.

note: A lively and largely accurate rendering of the Lokānanda scene with the rākṣasa, with a few misreadings of dramatic conventions and terms.
